name: m5-zd-clean-tip-prof
description: Does the Scala 2.13.x tip built with the release optimiser remove the indirect cost that Zinc's default mode adds to scalac's own phases? In `m5-zd-clean-prof`, `actor`'s typer and transform were 122 ms/op slower in default mode, led by the `itable stub` of the typer's self-type dispatch, which [scala/scala#11367](https://github.com/scala/scala/pull/11367) (merged into 2.13.x) devirtualises.

Zinc is sbt/zinc develop with the clean build mode ([retronym/zinc#100](https://github.com/retronym/zinc/pull/100), `dev-cb`). Scala is 2.13.18 from Maven (built with the release optimiser) or the 2.13.x tip 762d80f, built locally with `enableOptimizer` and published to ~/.ivy2/local. One compile at a time of Pekko 1.7.1 `actor` and `stream`.

The tip's compiler bridge is compiled from develop's bridge sources against the tip: the published `compiler-bridge_2.13` (compiled against 2.13.16) fails on the tip with `NoSuchMethodError: StdAttachments$MacroExpansionAttachment.$outer()` returning `Analyzer`, from `xsbt.GlobalHelpers.processMacroExpansion`, since #11367 changed the attachment's outer type.
Profile: async-profiler cpu and alloc, 2 forks per variant and project.

variantDescriptions.r18-clean: Scala 2.13.18 (Maven); Zinc clean build mode, no analysis
